author: Forbes
description:
The Trump administration is poised to institute a sweeping round of changes to how the Small Business Administration approves guaranteed loans of all sizes. The 416 pages of revised rules, which take effect on Oct. 1, are likely to roil small business investors, while also shrinking default rates and lessening the overall risk of SBA loans. For some borrowers, and in particular those buying businesses worth $350,000 or less, the changes will also mean more paperwork and longer waits for loan approvals, experts say.

The new standard operating procedure, or SOP, issued on Aug. 14, contains dozens of regulatory updates that will directly affect loan approval processing, particularly for loans being used to acquire businesses. That means there will likely be several weeks of confusion as loan applicants and bankers alike adjust to the new restrictions, experts told Forbes.

Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnschroyer/2026/09/22/big-changes-and-more-paperwork-
title: Big Changes And More Paperwork Coming To SBA Loans On Oct. 1

description:
In this episode of Excellence Across Generations, Steve and Moira Forbes sit down with Stew Leonard Jr. and his daughter, Blake Leonard, to uncover the raw, unfiltered reality of managing a multi-generational grocery empire. Thrust into the role of President at just 35, Stew Jr. had to learn how to run the business—and fast. He candidly discusses navigating a highly publicized IRS raid that sent his father to prison, and how an unimaginably tragic personal loss profoundly reshaped his approach to leadership, fatherhood, and business survival.

Now, as he prepares to pass the reins to his daughter, Blake, and his nephew, his biggest challenge is learning to step back and let them lead.
